Edit source parses with the same engine, so it refuses the same, at its place in the edited text. Still accepted though browsers refuse them (engine/README.md, open findings): a DOCTYPE's internal subset is read only for its entity declarations, not checked (a -- in one of its comments, stray text, a parameter-entity reference), a colon in a processing instruction's target, a name character outside XML's (a×b), an XML declaration's own syntax (no version, a version other than 1.x, an encoding that isn't a name, a standalone other than yes or no), a public identifier with a character XML doesn't allow there, and a namespace name that isn't a URI. The line has no fill; edit its stroke color (no "none" option), stroke-width (0-40) and stroke-linecap (butt / round / square).
Polygon has one handle per vertex; the points list shows every x,y pair as tokens.
Recolor the fill of rect, circle, ellipse or polygon (palette, custom or none).
Goal "Make a square": rect selected with width equal to height (within 0.5).
Goal "Round the corners": rect rx of 6 or more.
Goal "Ellipse into a circle": ellipse selected with rx equal to ry (within 0.5).
Chips switch the circle between a solid fill and a gradient fill. Gradient adds <defs><linearGradient id="sun"> running top to bottom (x1 0, y1 0, x2 0, y2 1) and sets the circle fill to url(#sun).
Edit both gradient stops: offset (0-1, step 0.05) and stop-color (no "none").
Pick the circle solid fill color (or none).
Pick the circle stroke color (or none) and its stroke-width (0-20).
A zigzag polyline with fill none: edit its stroke color and stroke-width (0-20).
Cycle stroke-linecap through butt / round / square.
Cycle stroke-linejoin through miter / round / bevel.

rows.name: Goal "Gradient fill": gradient fill switched on.
Tap the artboard to append a point; each new point after the first adds a straight L segment.
Each straight segment has a bend handle at its midpoint; dragging it turns the segment into a Q curve that passes through the finger.
Tapping a bend handle (without dragging) converts that segment to a Q curve with the control point pushed off to one side.

Tap a segment command letter in the code to cycle L -> Q -> C -> L; the geometry converts (L to Q places a control off the midpoint, Q to C degree-elevates exactly, C to Q approximates, back to L drops the controls).
Drag any anchor handle (the first is drawn as a filled start square); cubic control points attached to it move along. On a closed path whose last point equals the first, both move together.
Drag the control-point handles of Q (one) and C (two) segments.
Guide lines connect each curve control point to its anchors.
Every point and control coordinate is a number token (-50 to 150) labelled "point N x/y" or "control x/y".
"Close with Z" toggles a closing Z (the chip shows pressed while closed); undoing below 3 points reopens the path.
"Undo point" removes the last point and its segment.
"Clear" empties the path; an empty artboard shows "Tap to add a point".
"Try" chips load a preset path: Heart (closed, four C curves, filled and stroked), Wave (two C curves, open) and Check mark (two L segments).
Edit the path fill (or none), stroke (or none) and stroke-width (0-40).
Cycle stroke-linecap (butt / round / square) and stroke-linejoin (miter / round / bevel).
Goal "Add 3 points": three points added by tapping.
Goal "Bend a line": any segment is Q or C.
Goal "Close it with Z": the path is closed.
Goal "Fill it": the path is closed and its fill is not none.
A <g> holds a small house (two rects and a polygon drawn around 0,0) under one transform list: translate(tx ty) rotate(deg) scale(k).
Drag the center handle to translate the group (tooltip "translate(x y)").
Drag the drawing itself to translate it by whole units.
Drag the rotation handle above the house to rotate it in whole degrees (tooltip "rotate(N)").
Drag the diamond scale handle; scale snaps to 0.05 steps between 0.2 and 4 (tooltip "scale(N)").
Every transform number is a token: translate x/y (-20 to 120), rotate (-360 to 360) and scale (0.1-4, step 0.05). The list prints one function per line.
A local grid and red x/y axes are drawn inside the same transform, so the coordinate system visibly moves, spins and scales with the group.
Recolor the three child shapes (walls, roof, door).
Goal "Turn it upside down": rotation is 180 degrees (mod 360, within 2).
Goal "Park it top right": translate x 75 or more and y 25 or less.
Pulse: a circle whose radius animates between two values and back.
Edit the two pulse radii (1-50); the first value is shared by circle r and the start/end of values.
Spin: a rounded square with animateTransform type="rotate" from "0 50 50" to "N 50 50"; the end angle is a token (-1080 to 1080, step 15).
Slide: a circle whose cx animates between two x positions (0-100) and back.
In Slide, cycle calcMode through linear / spline / discrete; spline adds keyTimes "0;0.5;1" and ease-in-out keySplines.
Draw: a check-mark path with pathLength 100 and stroke-dasharray 100 whose stroke-dashoffset animates 100 to 0, so the line draws itself.
Color: a circle whose fill animates between two colors and back; both colors are tokens.
Edit dur for the current motion (0.1-10 s, step 0.1).
Cycle repeatCount through indefinite / 1 / 3; changing it restarts the animation.
Each motion has its own shape color token (fill, or stroke for Draw).
Pause / Play freezes or resumes all SMIL animation on the artboard.
Replay restarts the timeline from 0 (and resumes if paused).
While paused (the default under reduced motion) the artboard shows the end of a cycle, so Draw is fully drawn rather than empty.
Goal "Try 3 motions": three different motions opened.
Goal "Speed up (dur under 1s)": the current motion has dur below 1.
Goal "Play once": the current motion has repeatCount 1.
The data lives in an XML comment ("data: 30, 55, ...") whose values (0-100) are editable tokens; a second comment states the rule "height = value x 0.8, y = 90 - height".
Each bar (or line point) has a handle at its top; drag it up or down to set that value (0-100, tooltip "value N").
Bar x, y, width, height, label positions and label text are read-only numbers computed from the data; they update as the data changes.
Bars: one rect per value on a baseline line, each with a small centred value label (font-size 5, sans-serif).
Line: the same data as a polyline (fill none, stroke-width 2, round joins) with a circle dot and label at each point.
One color token colors every bar, or the line and its dots.
"Add bar" appends a random value (multiple of 5) up to 10 bars; bar widths re-space to fit.
"Shuffle" replaces every value with a random multiple of 5.
Goal "Add a bar": 6 or more values.
Goal "Switch to a line": line mode.
Icon template: a rounded dark square (rect rx 18) with a closed cubic-Bezier heart path on top.
Logo template: a yellow circle, an open quadratic wave path (stroke 4, round caps) and bold "SUNWAVE" text (font-weight 900, text-anchor middle).
Scene template: a full-bleed sky rect, a sun circle, a cloud ellipse and a bird path that float (animateTransform translate), and two closed hill paths (one Q, one C).
rows.note: template chip. Re-phased from P1 (Mark, 2026-09-29): its floating shapes are animation, which arrives in P5.

rows.name: "Name it" opens a text sheet. A name adds <title id="drawing-title"> as the first child and role="img" plus aria-labelledby="drawing-title" on the root <svg>; the title text is also an editable text token. Clearing it removes both.
Rect tool adds a 40x30 rect (rx 0, no stroke) in the next palette color; each new shape is offset so it does not sit exactly on the last.
Circle tool adds an r 18 circle in the next palette color.
Ellipse tool adds a 26x14 ellipse in the next palette color.
Line tool adds a diagonal line (stroke in the next palette color, width 4, round caps).
Text tool adds "Hello" (size 14, sans-serif, weight 700, middle, dark fill) and opens the text sheet at once.

Pen starts an empty open path (stroke width 3, round caps and joins, no fill); each tap on the artboard adds a straight point. Bend handles are hidden while drawing. A "Tap to add points" hint shows in the toolbar.
While drawing, "Undo point" (or the Undo button / Cmd-Z) removes the last point.
After 3 points, "Close" or tapping the first point closes the path with Z and ends the pen.
"Done", Enter or Escape ends the pen; a path with fewer than 2 points is discarded.
Tap a shape to select it (lines get a wider hit zone); tap empty artboard, press Escape or "Deselect" to clear. A dashed bounding box marks the selection and its code block is highlighted.
Tap an element block in the code to select that shape on the artboard.
Drag any shape to move it by whole units; a tooltip shows its center.
The selected shape shows its handles: rect top-left and bottom-right, circle center and radius, ellipse center, rx and ry, line ends, text position, and one per vertex for a pasted polygon.
A selected path shows anchor handles, Q/C control handles with arms, and bend handles on straight segments (drag to curve, tap to convert to Q). Moving an anchor carries its cubic controls.

Every attribute of every shape is a live token: coordinates and sizes scrub, fill and stroke open the color sheet, segment type (L/Q/C), linecap, linejoin, font-family, font-weight and text-anchor cycle, and text opens the text sheet. Setting a stroke on a stroke-less shape gives it width 2.
Text exposes x, y, font-size (2-80), font-family (sans-serif / serif / monospace), font-weight (400 / 700 / 900), text-anchor (start / middle / end), fill and its string.
Fill swatch (every kind except line and raw items) opens the color sheet: 16-color palette, none and a custom color.
Stroke swatch (every kind except text and raw items) opens the color sheet plus a stroke-width slider (0-20). "none" is offered except for lines.
"Edit text" (text only) opens the text sheet (60 characters max).
For a path, "Close" / "Open" toggles the closing Z.

"Arrows" (line or open path) cycles none -> arrow at end -> both ends. It generates a per-shape <marker id="arrow-N"> (viewBox 0 0 10 10, refX 8, refY 5, size 3, orient auto-start-reverse, a triangle filled with the stroke color) and marker-end / marker-start; a stroke is added if missing.
rows.note: toolbar button. Re-phased from P1 (Mark, 2026-09-29): markers arrive in P3.

rows.name: "Gloss" (not line, text or raw items) swaps the fill for a per-shape <radialGradient id="gloss-N"> (cx 0.35, cy 0.3, r 0.8) from white to the fill color; the end color stays editable as the fill token. A shape with no fill gets one.

"Motion" (not raw items) cycles none -> spin -> float -> fade (-> draw for paths). Spin = animateTransform rotate 0 to 360 around the shape center (read-only cx cy); float = animateTransform translate "0 0;0 -5;0 0"; fade = animate opacity "1;0.2;1"; draw = animate stroke-dashoffset "100;0" with pathLength 100 and stroke-dasharray 100 (adds a stroke if missing). All repeat indefinitely; turning motion on resumes playback.
The animation dur is a number token (0.2-30 s, step 0.1). Defaults: spin 4, float 3, fade 2, draw 2.
"Autoplay" / "On tap" toggles begin="click"; tapping the shape in the editor previews the start.

"Effect" (not raw items) cycles none -> shadow -> glow -> blur -> wobble. Each is a per-shape <filter> (filterUnits userSpaceOnUse, x -10, y -10, 120x120): feDropShadow (dx 2, dy 3, stdDeviation 2, flood-opacity 0.35); feGaussianBlur 3 merged under the source; feGaussianBlur 2; feTurbulence + feDisplacementMap (scale 4).
rows.note: toolbar button. Re-phased from P1 (Mark, 2026-09-29): filters arrive in P4.

rows.name: "Duplicate" inserts a copy just above the original, offset by 5,5, and selects it.
"Forward" and "Back" swap the shape with its neighbour in document order (later paints on top).
"Delete" (or the Delete / Backspace key) removes the selected shape.
Undo and Redo buttons on the artboard (also Cmd/Ctrl-Z, Shift-Cmd-Z, Cmd/Ctrl-Y) step through up to 80 snapshots; they disable at either end.
The grid button on the artboard shows or hides the background grid (Create only).
The play/pause button on the artboard pauses all motion. While paused, animation elements stay in the code but are not rendered. Starts paused under reduced motion.
The code panel Edit button opens the exported code in a textarea; Apply parses it back into editable shapes, or shows "That code couldn't be read..." when the XML is malformed.

Pasted rect, circle, ellipse, line, polygon, path and text become editable shapes when they use only their geometry attributes plus fill, stroke, stroke-width, stroke-linecap, stroke-linejoin, marker-start/end and filter. A missing fill defaults to black.
A pasted path d is editable when it is a single subpath of M, L, H, V, Q, C and a final Z, absolute or relative (H and V become L). A, S, T or a second M make the element raw.

The editor's own output round-trips: a <defs> made only of gloss-N gradients, arrow-N markers and shadow/glow/blur/wobble-N filters becomes gloss / arrows / effect toggles again; a leading <title> becomes the name; one SMIL child with repeatCount indefinite and begin 0, 0s or click becomes a motion.
rows.note: code button + sheet field. Re-phased from P1 (Mark, 2026-09-29): it turns the arrows (P3), effects (P4) and motion (P5) it names back into toggles, so it lands with the last of them.

rows.name: Anything else pasted (groups, use, gradients, extra attributes, etc.) is kept as a raw item: sanitized, rendered, shown verbatim in code, selectable, duplicable, reorderable and deletable, but not movable or restylable.
Copy or Download exports the drawing as a standalone file with xmlns (Download names it my-drawing.svg).
The drawing and its name are saved to localStorage after each change and restored next visit; if a render fails, the drawing resets to empty.
An empty artboard shows "Add a shape below".
Keyboard: Escape deselects (or ends the pen), Enter ends the pen, Delete/Backspace deletes, Cmd/Ctrl-Z undo, Shift-Cmd-Z or Cmd/Ctrl-Y redo.
Goal "Draw a curve": some path has a Q or C segment.
Goal "Add motion": some item has a motion.
Goal "Copy or download": the drawing was copied or downloaded.
Arcs: one elliptical arc "M x y A rx ry rotation large-arc sweep x y". Every number is a token: start/end (0-100), rx and ry (1-100), rotation (-180 to 180). A comment spells out the parameter order.
Drag the start (filled square) and end handles of the arc.
Tap the large-arc flag to flip it between 0 and 1.
Tap the sweep flag to flip it between 0 and 1.
The three other arcs the same endpoints and radii allow are drawn as dashed ghosts; tap one to switch the flags to it.
Each arc is labelled at its midpoint with its "large sweep" flag pair; the chosen arc's label is highlighted.
Edit the arc stroke color and stroke-width (1-12); caps are round.
Donut: a data comment holds four editable values (1-100).
Each slice is its own stroked arc path (radius 28, stroke-width 14, fill none, sweep 1) with read-only start/end points. Its large-arc flag is computed: 1 when the slice is over half.
Drag the handles on the boundaries between slices around the ring; the two neighbouring values trade amounts (each stays at least 1). Tooltip "a | b".
Recolor each slice from its stroke token.
Percentage labels sit outside each slice.
Smooth: S / T chips switch between "M C S" (cubic plus smooth cubic) and "M Q T" (quadratic plus smooth quadratic).
Drag every point: start, middle and end anchors plus the control points.
Arms connect controls to anchors. A dashed arm and a dashed dot show the mirrored control point that S or T implies at the middle point.
"Relative" rewrites the path in lowercase (m c s / m q t): each number becomes an offset from its reference point, and editing a relative anchor shifts everything drawn after it.
Edit the smooth path stroke color and stroke-width (1-12).
Holes: one path draws an outer circle (two arcs) and an inner keyhole subpath (arc plus lines), each closed with Z. A comment names each direction.
Cycle fill-rule between nonzero and evenodd to see whether the inner shape cuts a hole.
"Reverse inner shape" rewrites the inner subpath counter-clockwise, so nonzero also cuts the hole.
Arrowheads on the artboard show each subpath's drawing direction.
Goal "Try all 4 arcs": all four flag combinations seen.
Goal "A slice over half": any donut value is more than half the total.
Goal "Cut the hole 2 ways": used evenodd, and used nonzero with the inner shape reversed.
Three <symbol>s (star, heart, bolt), each with viewBox 0 0 24 24 and one path, are defined once in <defs>.
Edit a symbol's path stroke (or none) and stroke-width (0-6, step 0.5) once; every copy that uses it updates.
Five <use href="#icon-..."> copies place the symbols at their own x, y and size.
Drag a copy to move it (tooltip "x N, y N"); its x and y (-20 to 120) are also tokens.
A selected copy shows a corner handle that resizes it as a square (6-90); width and height share one token (4-100).
Each copy has its own fill color (or none), which the symbol's unfilled path inherits.
Tap a copy's href to cycle it through #icon-star, #icon-heart and #icon-bolt.
Tap a copy (or its line in the code) to select it; a dashed box marks it. Tap empty artboard to deselect.
"Add copy" adds a copy with the next symbol, a random position and size and a palette color (up to 12).
"Remove copy" removes the selected copy, or the last one (keeps at least 1).
Goal "Edit a symbol once": some symbol stroke or width changed.
Goal "Swap an icon": some copy's href changed.
Goal "Add a copy": 6 or more copies.
Radial gradient: a circle filled with url(#gloss), a radialGradient with three stops.
Drag the center handle to move cx, cy (in 0-1 bounding-box units).
Drag the edge handle to set r (0.02-2); a dashed circle shows it.
Drag the pink highlight handle to move the focal point fx, fy; it is kept inside the gradient circle.
cx, cy, r, fx and fy are also tokens (step 0.01).
Cycle spreadMethod through pad / reflect / repeat.
Three stops: offsets 0 and 1 are fixed, the middle offset is a token (0-1). All three stop colors are editable.
A dashed box labelled "0,0" and "1,1" shows the bounding-box units the gradient numbers use.
Pattern: a <pattern id="hatch"> tile (paper rect plus one stripe rect) fills the last two bars of a bar chart; the first three stay solid.
Edit the tile size (2-20); it sets the pattern width and height and the height of both tile rects.
Edit the paper color, the stripe color and the stripe width (0.5-10).
Dashed outlines show a 3x3 block of rotated tile cells over the fourth bar.
Goal "Move the highlight": fx or fy changed.
Goal "Try reflect or repeat": spreadMethod not pad.
Goal "Make them denser": tile size 4 or less.
The full landscape is drawn faintly (opacity 0.15) behind the result, on the artboard only (not in the code).
Keyhole: a <clipPath id="peek"> holding a keyhole path shows only that part of the landscape group (clip-path url(#peek)).
Drag anywhere, or drag the center handle, to move the keyhole; its translate x/y (-20 to 120) are tokens.
rows.note: drag shape + drag handle + scrub token

rows.name: Drag the diamond scale handle to resize the keyhole (0.3-5); the scale is a token.
Text: the clipPath holds a heavy text (sans-serif, 900, middle), so the landscape shows through the letters. Tap the word in the code to change it.
Move the clip text by dragging or with its center handle; x, y (-20 to 120) and font-size (6-80) are tokens.
rows.note: drag shape + drag handle + scrub token

rows.name: Fade: a <mask> holding a rect filled with a vertical linearGradient; brightness decides visibility (white shows, black hides).
Edit the two mask gradient stops: offset (0-1) and color (gray gives partial visibility).
Wipe: an animated mask whose rect width animates 0 to 100, revealing the scene; its duration (0.2-10 s) and color are tokens.
rows.note: mode chip + scrub token + tap token

rows.name: In Wipe, a Play / Pause chip. Under reduced motion it opens paused, showing the wipe half way.
Goal "Move the keyhole": keyhole position changed.
Goal "Clip to your own word": clip text is not "SVG" and not empty.
Goal "Fade with a mask": the Fade mode was opened.
Goal "Half-hide with gray": a mask color that is neither pure white nor pure black.
Flowchart: a <marker id="arrow"> (viewBox 0 0 10 10, refY 5) holding a triangle path is attached to connector lines with marker-end; one two-way link also uses marker-start.
Edit refX (-5 to 15) to slide the arrow tip along the line; 10 puts the tip exactly on the line end.
Edit the marker size (1-20); markerWidth and markerHeight share one token.
Cycle orient through auto-start-reverse / auto / 0 to see how the start arrow turns.
Drag a flowchart box (a translated group with a rounded rect and a label) to move it; the connecting lines follow. Its translate numbers are also tokens.
Connector endpoints are read-only numbers computed to stop at the box edges.
Line chart: a <marker id="dot"> (a white circle ringed in the line color) sits on the points of a polyline through marker-start, marker-mid and marker-end.
Toggle each of marker-start, marker-mid and marker-end between url(#dot) and none.
Edit the dot marker size (1-12) and the line color (it colors the line and the dot rings).
Drag near a line point, up or down, to change its value; the polyline points are read-only numbers.
Goal "Tip on the line end": refX is 10.
Goal "Flip the start arrow": orient auto used.
Goal "Move a box": a box moved.
Goal "Dots in the middle only": marker-start and marker-end none, marker-mid on.
Text on a path: a <textPath href="#ring"> runs text around a circular path defined in <defs>.
The ring is a circle written as two relative arcs ("m -r 0 a r r 0 1 1 2r 0 ..."). The radius is a token (8-48) and the diameter is derived read-only.
Drag the radius handle to grow or shrink the ring (12-48); the center dot shrinks with it.
Drag the pink dot around the ring to slide the text; startOffset (-100 to 200%) is also a token.
Edit font-size (3-20) and letter-spacing (-2 to 10, step 0.5); weight is 700, anchor middle.
Recolor the text and the center dot.
A dashed circle, an arrowhead and a "start" label show where and which way the path begins.
Lines: one <text> with a <tspan> per line; each tspan repeats x so it returns to the left margin.
Each line's dy (-3 to 5 em, step 0.1) moves it down from the line before.
Lines can carry their own style: the second is big (font-size 14, weight 900), the third has its own fill color token.
"Add line" appends "new line" (up to 7); "Remove line" drops the last (keeps 1).
Drag the center handle to move the whole block; x (shared by the text and every tspan) and y (-20 to 120) are tokens.
Goal "Write your own badge": badge text changed.
Goal "Add a line": 4 or more lines.
Goal "Loosen the lines": some line after the first has dy 1.6 or more.
An inline <style> block styles the drawing by class: .logo, .logo.night, .tile, .glyph, .caption and .glyph:hover.
Color values inside the CSS (color and --paper for .logo and .logo.night) are tokens that open the color sheet.
The heart glyph and the caption use fill: currentColor, so one color value restyles both.
The tile fill comes from a CSS custom property: .tile { fill: var(--paper) }.
"Toggle .night" (or tapping the group class in the code) switches the group between "logo" and "logo night", swapping both colors at once.
"Toggle .tile" (or tapping the rect class) switches between "tile" and "plain"; plain lets the rect's presentation attribute fill="#8d99ae" win, showing that CSS beats attributes.
A .glyph:hover rule dims the heart on hover (live on the artboard); its opacity (0-1) is a token.
Goal "Recolor with one value": the .logo color changed.
Goal "Switch on .night": the night class is on.
Goal "Let the attribute win": rect class is plain.
A plane (drawn around 0,0) flies along a dashed route with <animateMotion>; a comment explains that animateMotion carries the 0,0 origin along the path.
Drag six route handles (start, middle, end anchors and three control points) to reshape the route "M C S"; the plane follows it.
Every route coordinate (-20 to 120) is a token.
Arms plus a dashed arm and dot show the control point that S mirrors at the middle point.
"Use <mpath>" switches between <mpath href="#route"> (reusing the drawn path by id) and a copy of the path data in animateMotion's path attribute.
Cycle rotate through auto / auto-reverse / 0: whether the plane turns with the curve.
Edit dur (0.5-30 s, step 0.5); the timeline slider range follows it.
A timeline slider (0 to dur) shows the current time; dragging it pauses and seeks the animation.
Play / Pause stops or resumes the animation (opens paused under reduced motion).
A readout shows the current time in seconds (e.g. "2.4s").
Recolor the plane fill and the route stroke (route stroke may be none); the route is dashed "3 3".
Goal "Reshape the route": a route point moved.
Goal "Slow it down": dur 9 s or more.
Goal "Scrub the timeline": the slider was used.
Traffic light: tap the Go button in the drawing; the red light's <set> begins on "go.click" (an event on another element).
Cycle the red light's begin between go.click and 0s (start at load); changing it restarts the timeline.
Each step starts when the one before it ends: amber begins on red.end, green and the car on amber.end.
Each light is a <set attributeName="fill" to="..."> that switches color for its dur.
Green stays on until the next Go tap (end="go.click").
Edit the red and amber durations and the car's drive time (0.2-10 s, step 0.1).
A car group drives right with animateTransform type translate (0 0 to 34 0) when amber ends.
Cycle the car animation's fill between freeze (stays parked) and remove (snaps back).
Replay resets the timeline to 0 and redraws.

set vs discard: tap each balloon. One removes itself with <discard begin="click">, the other hides with <set attributeName="display" to="none" begin="click">. Comments note that discard was removed from the spec.
A live test reports whether this browser acts on <discard>, printed on the artboard.
Goal "Start it with a tap": Go tapped.
Goal "Change a step": red or amber duration changed.
Goal "Let the car snap back": fill remove.
Goal "Pop the set balloon": the set balloon was tapped.

A spinner arc: a stroked circle (r 28, stroke-width 8, round caps) over a grey track, with stroke-dasharray "dash gap"; dash (5-170) is a token and gap is derived read-only so dash + gap is the circumference.
SMIL: an animateTransform rotate from "0 50 50" to "360 50 50" repeating indefinitely; dur (0.2-10 s) is a token.
CSS: a <style> with .arc { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; animation: turn Ns ease infinite } and @keyframes turn to rotate(360deg); the duration is a token.
Cycle the CSS timing function through linear / ease-in-out / steps(8).
JavaScript: a <script> that rotates #arc with requestAnimationFrame; the milliseconds per turn (200-10000, step 50) is a token. The lab runs a matching loop itself; the code is not executed.
One speed value drives all three versions (seconds in SMIL and CSS, milliseconds in JS).
Pause / Play: pauses SMIL, sets animation-play-state paused for CSS, and stops the JS loop. Opens paused under reduced motion; the hint notes CSS animation is off under reduced motion.
Goal "Try all three": SMIL, CSS and JavaScript each opened.
Goal "Change the speed": duration not 1 s.
Goal "Try another easing": easing not linear.
Links: six continent polygons, each wrapped in <a href target>; href is an editable text token (defaults to Wikipedia pages).
Tapping a region stays in the lab: the region is outlined and named, and a bar under the artboard says where it links (and "in a new tab" for _blank), with an Open chip for http(s) links.
A <style> rule "a:hover polygon, a:focus polygon { fill: ... }" highlights regions; the hover color is a token.
Script: a <script> adds a handler to every bar that moves a hidden tooltip group next to it, sets its text from data-v and makes it visible. The lab mirrors the script live.
Cycle the listened event between click and pointerenter.

Inline vs : the same file shown twice. Inline, its script runs (a caption reports whether it did); as an it runs in secure animated mode, so animation plays but scripts and taps do not. The file carries xmlns.
In the comparison, tapping the inline badge runs <set attributeName="fill" begin="click">; its color is a token.
The badge star spins with animateTransform rotate; its dur (0.5-30 s) is a token.
The script sets the note text to an editable message ("script ran") and recolors it.
In the comparison, Play / Pause stops both panes by adding begin="indefinite" to looping animations (the code shown is unchanged).

Grain: feTurbulence type fractalNoise; baseFrequency (0.05-2), numOctaves (1-6) and seed (0-99) are tokens.

Wobble: feTurbulence type turbulence (baseFrequency 0.005-0.5, seed tokens) drives feDisplacementMap (scale 0-30, channels R and G), bending a line drawing.
"Boil" adds an <animate attributeName="seed" values="1;2;3" dur="0.3s" calcMode="discrete" repeatCount="indefinite"> inside feTurbulence, so the wobble flickers.
